stem: A client has taken metformin for several years and now reports fatigue and new numbness and tingling in the feet. Which long-term medication-related problem should the nurse consider and evaluate?

options.A: Iron overload caused by cumulative metformin exposure.
options.B: Vitamin C toxicity caused by increased vitamin C absorption.
options.C: Vitamin B12 deficiency associated with long-term metformin therapy.
options.D: Folate excess as the characteristic cause of neuropathy during metformin therapy.

rationale: The current metformin extended-release label warns that metformin can lower vitamin B12 concentrations and directs annual hematologic monitoring plus vitamin B12 measurement every 2 to 3 years. NIH Office of Dietary Supplements guidance also identifies prolonged metformin use as a cause of vitamin B12 deficiency and notes that deficiency can cause fatigue and neurologic symptoms such as numbness and tingling of the hands and feet. Therefore C should be considered and evaluated. A, B, and D are not recognized characteristic nutritional complications of metformin therapy.
educational_objective: Recognize vitamin B12 deficiency as a long-term metformin-associated problem and evaluate compatible hematologic or neurologic symptoms with appropriate B12 and hematologic monitoring.
source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. Food and Drug Administration labeling; NIH Office of Dietary Supplements
source_document_title: Metformin Hydrochloride Extended-Release Tablets; Vitamin B12 Fact Sheet for Health Professionals
source_version_date: Metformin label updated July 1, 2026 and revised July 2026; NIH ODS Vitamin B12 professional fact sheet current in 2026
source_locator: DailyMed Warnings and Precautions §5.2 Vitamin B12 Deficiency: metformin may lower B12; measure hematologic parameters annually and B12 every 2-3 years. NIH ODS > Vitamin B12 Deficiency: prolonged metformin use is a recognized cause; deficiency can cause fatigue and numbness/tingling in hands and feet.
source_claim_supported: Long-term metformin can lower vitamin B12; fatigue with distal numbness/tingling is compatible with B12 deficiency and warrants evaluation rather than attribution to unrelated nutritional toxicities.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — metformin-associated vitamin B12 deficiency

source_original.stem: A client has taken metformin for several years and now reports fatigue and new distal paresthesias. Which long-term adverse effect should be considered?

options.A: Iron overload is a recognized cumulative effect of metformin and commonly produces distal paresthesias.
options.B: Vitamin C toxicity is expected after prolonged metformin use because the drug increases vitamin C absorption.
options.C: Vitamin B12 deficiency should be considered during long-term metformin therapy, particularly with compatible hematologic or neurologic findings.
options.D: Folate excess is the characteristic nutritional complication responsible for neuropathy during metformin therapy.

source_original.rationale: Metformin labeling recognizes decreased vitamin B12 concentrations during treatment and recommends periodic hematologic monitoring, with vitamin B12 assessment when clinically indicated. Fatigue and paresthesias are compatible with B12 deficiency and warrant evaluation.
source_original.source_detail: Warnings and Precautions §5.2 — Vitamin B12 Deficiency. Revised 07/2026, version 8; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: medication administration, adverse effects/interactions, monitoring, reconciliation and teaching. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the vitamin-B12 construct and key C, translated paresthesias into candidate-facing numbness/tingling, added NIH ODS corroboration for the symptom pattern, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium because the final item tests a direct long-term medication adverse effect plus compatible symptoms.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current DailyMed/FDA metformin label plus NIH ODS symptom/cause guidance; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: Metformin label updated 2026-07-01/revised 07/2026; NIH ODS currentness live-rechecked 2026-08-16
audit_findings.exact_locator: DailyMed §5.2 Vitamin B12 Deficiency; NIH ODS Vitamin B12 Deficiency section
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item asks the nurse to consider/evaluate B12 deficiency rather than diagnosing it from nonspecific symptoms. The medication association and compatible neurologic/fatigue symptoms are directly supported.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect; iron overload is not a characteristic cumulative metformin toxicity.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect; metformin does not characteristically produce vitamin C toxicity through increased absorption.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect; folate excess is not the characteristic nutritional complication of metformin and does not explain the recognized B12 association.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C links the known long-term metformin effect to the compatible neurologic/fatigue presentation without asserting an unsupported diagnosis.
audit_findings.cueing: All answers are nutritional/metabolic interpretations, so the key depends on the medication-specific evidence rather than an unrelated clue.
audit_findings.blueprint: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — long-term adverse-effect monitoring and laboratory evaluation.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked the July 2026 metformin label, NIH ODS deficiency manifestations and metformin association, all options, rationale, objective, difficulty, ambiguity, cueing and NCSBN mapping. C remained uniquely correct.
